## Problem statement

The [weftspun/see-through-cpp](https://github.com/weftspun/see-through-cpp) pipeline decomposes a single anime illustration into semantically layered PSD output. It currently runs on ggml (C++ GPU backends). We need a verified, portable implementation using Lean 4 for formal kernel correctness and Slang for portable GPU compute.

## Goals

1. **Correctness by construction**: Every GPU compute kernel is emitted from Lean 4 via [lean-slang](https://github.com/V-Sekai-fire/lean-slang), verified with `native_decide` reference fixtures, and cross-checked against a CPU harness.

2. **Portable weights**: Model weights from [shitagaki-lab/see-through](https://github.com/shitagaki-lab/see-through) (HuggingFace safetensors) are consumed directly at original dtype.

3. **Performant**: Slang → `slangc -target spirv` → Vulkan GPU dispatch on NVIDIA/AMD; Slang → Metal Shading Language path for Apple Silicon.

## Repository layout

```
see-through-verify/
├── decisions/               # Decision records (this book)
├── Compute/                 # Lean Slang compute shader modules
│   ├── Gemm.lean            # f32×f32 GEMM
│   ├── Conv2d.lean          # f32×f32 direct conv2d
│   └── Verify.lean          # native_decide reference fixtures
├── shaders/                 # Slang shader sources
│   └── cpp/                 # slangc -target cpp exports (CPU-validation)
├── Runtime/                 # GPU runtime harness
├── lakefile.lean
└── LICENSE
```

## Weight pipeline

```
shitagaki-lab/see-through (HuggingFace safetensors)  →  Compute/Safetensors.lean
        ─ or direct ggml GGUF oracle taps for validation
```

Weights flow: HuggingFace safetensors → `Compute/Safetensors.lean` reads
directly (original dtype, no widening). Slang shaders load raw bytes and
reinterpret based on metadata.

## Compute shader modules

| Shader | Role |
| ------ | ---- |
| GEMM | C[M,N] = A[M,K] × B[K,N] — foundation for all linears, convs, attention |
| Direct conv2d | out[oc,oh,ow] = Σ_c Σ_kh Σ_kw in[c,oh·s+kh,ow·s+kw] × w[c,oc,kh,kw] |
| MHA attention | QK^T / sqrt(hd) softmax PV, per-head workspace |
| LayerNorm / GroupNorm | Normalization for transformer blocks & resnets |
| GEGLU | LayerNorm GEGLU FFN (gate in 2nd half) |

All kernels are authored in Slang and exported to C++ via `slangc -target cpp`
(per-thread, no barriers), then validated against ggml oracle taps — no
hand-coded C++. Live verification status (which kernels are GREEN) is tracked
in [RFD 0006](0006-cli-parity.qmd); the critical-path plan and its PERT diagram
are both in [RFD 0006](0006-cli-parity.qmd).

## GPU dispatch

The runtime flow:

1. **Compile time** (Lean): `Compute/Gemm.lean` → `LeanSlang.emit` → `.slang` source
2. **Build time** (slangc): `slangc -target cpp` → `.cpp` for CPU validation, `-target spirv` / `-target metal` for GPU
3. **Launch time** (C++/Rust harness): bind weight buffers, `vkCmdDispatch` the shaders in pipeline order, read back results.

The CPU cpp path is the verification anchor: if CPU C++ output matches the GPU
(SPIR-V and/or Metal) output, the shader is provably correct on all targets
because they are generated from the same source.

## Verification gate

Kernel correctness is validated by comparing Slang-exported output against
ggml oracle taps, gating on `cos > 0.999` (GGUF-F16 vs safetensors-BF16 weight
rounding makes a strict `max_abs` gate too tight for chained stages). See
[RFD 0006](0006-cli-parity.qmd).
